requirements.quote: Every line is composed of two fields separated by a single TAB character (`\t`) and **nothing else**:
COUNT is the plain decimal integer (no padding or leading spaces).
Generate a frequency report that shows how many times every checksum string occurs in the list.

check.cmd: a=$(sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//' /home/user/data/daily_checksums.txt | grep -v '^$' | LC_ALL=C sort | uniq -c | LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1nr -k2,2 | awk '{printf "%s\t%s\n",$1,$2}'); b=$(cat /home/user/data/checksum_frequency.log); [ -n "$b" ] && [ "$a" = "$b" ]

requirements.quote: A final newline must follow the last line of the file.
